rationale: Start with a broad, strong scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the retention window without risking truncation. This gives a first read on overall hydrophobicity distribution and where compression or crowding occurs.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only gain left is reducing t_last below 10 min. Keep composition and temperature fixed and shorten the gradient to test how much runtime can be cut before the first critical pair begins to lose resolution.

The current method is nearly ideal, with the same 6/7 pair now limiting resolution. Take one more step steeper at the same endpoints and temperature to see whether t_last can be pushed under 10 min while keeping that pair at or above 1.5.

At 14 min the run is fast enough, and the only issue is the 6/7 pair falling below 1.5. Lowering temperature one step should increase retention/selectivity and recover that pair while likely keeping the last peak under 10 min.

The 16 min method at 40 C was very close to perfect, so probe the tradeoff in the other direction by raising temperature one step to reduce t_last while watching whether the critical midcluster remains fully resolved. This tests if we can beat the 16 min run without the stronger resolution loss seen at 14 min.

The problem at 14 min is localized compression in the midcluster, so raise only the starting organic one step to narrow early retention spacing differently while keeping the fast overall runtime. This tests whether reshaping the gradient window can recover the 6/7 pair without pushing the last peak back over 10 min.

Keep the promising fast 14 min, 40 C method but lower phi1 one step to flatten the gradient slightly and give the crowded midcluster a bit more separation leverage. This may lift the 6/7 pair toward full credit while likely keeping the last peak within 10 min.

Lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 improved the critical 6/7 pair while keeping t_last under 10 min, so take one more step in the same direction. This should further ease compression in the midcluster and may push the last unresolved pair to full credit.

You have reached full resolution, so now optimize purely for speed. Shorten the gradient one step while holding the successful composition window to see if all pairs remain at or above 1.5 and t_last drops clearly below 10 min.

Since 12 min was too steep but 14 min at phi1 0.85 was fully resolved, lower phi1 one more step at 14 min to see if the critical 6/7 pair gains extra margin while pulling the last peak slightly earlier than the current best. This explores whether a narrower gradient window can preserve CRF 1.000 with more speed headroom.

The best point is on the edge: fully resolved but with t_last just over 10 min. Raising phi0 one step while keeping phi1 and tG fixed should shift the whole window earlier and may retain full resolution if the critical midcluster is governed more by the upper part of the gradient.

This method now has full resolution with useful margin and the last peak comfortably under 10 min, so shorten tG one step to see whether that margin is enough to preserve full credit at faster runtime. The goal is to find the shortest still-fully-resolved condition and then back off if needed.

At phi0 0.15 and tG 14 min, resolution is just adequate; increasing phi1 one step should make the gradient slightly steeper overall and may move the last peak earlier while checking whether the critical 6/7 pair still stays above 1.5. This maps the local optimum around the current 1.000 method.

Raising phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 preserved full resolution and moved t_last earlier, so test one more step higher at the same successful phi1 and tG. This checks whether the whole window can be shifted earlier again while keeping the critical 6/7 pair above 1.5.

The current best is full resolution with some margin; lowering phi1 at phi0 0.15 may increase the critical 6/7 separation while possibly still keeping t_last below 10 min. This tests whether a slightly narrower gradient window can maintain CRF 1.000 but improve speed robustness around the optimum.

Two methods already achieve the maximum score, so use remaining budget to search for a shorter practical optimum. Raising temperature one step from the best 0.15/0.85/14 condition should pull t_last earlier; if the 6/7 pair stays at or above 1.5, this would also be a fully resolved but faster method.

Temperature has a strong effect on selectivity, but 45 C was too high; test the other direction from the proven 0.10/0.85/14 condition to see whether 35 C can retain full resolution while keeping t_last at or below 10 min. This is a targeted selectivity check near a current optimum, not a broad search.

The best methods are both at 14 min and 40 C; with maximum CRF already achieved, use remaining budget to map robustness around the optimum. A slightly shallower gradient should increase the margin on the critical 6/7 pair and confirm whether 0.15/0.85 is the more robust operating point.

Map the remaining corner near the optimum by combining the higher phi0 shift with the lower phi1 window. This could preserve or improve the critical 6/7 resolution while pulling the whole chromatogram earlier enough to stay under 10 min.

This new 1.000 method is a good candidate for a shorter optimum because it keeps full resolution with the last peak below 10 min. Shorten tG one step to test whether this shifted window can hold the critical 6/7 pair at or above 1.5 while reducing runtime further.

At phi0 0.20, the 14 min method is fully resolved and the 12 min version is just too steep, so lower phi1 one step at 14 min to increase margin on the critical 6/7 pair. This tests whether the same fast window can stay at CRF 1.000 with stronger robustness and possibly a similar t_last.

The 0.20/0.80/14 method is fully resolved with t_last 9.67 min, so push phi0 one more step higher while keeping the same upper endpoint. This probes whether the chromatogram can be shifted earlier again without losing the critical 6/7 pair, potentially identifying a shorter 1.000-equivalent operating point.

With only a few injections left and several 1.000 methods already found, target robustness around the fastest shifted optimum. A slightly shallower version of 0.20/0.85/14 should show whether that region offers more resolution margin on 6/7 while remaining a practical backup method.

This fills the last useful unexplored point around the successful 0.15/0.80 and 0.20/0.80 conditions. It may combine the stronger 6/7 resolution seen at lower phi1 with the better time performance from the higher phi0 shift, potentially yielding another robust CRF 1.000 method.

Use the final injection to complete the phi0 trend at the best phi1/tG/T setting. This will show whether lowering phi0 below the successful 0.10–0.20 range offers any improvement in selectivity or confirms that the optimum truly lies in the middle of that range.
